title: Maximum Units on a Truck
statement:
A warehouse manager has to load a truck. The warehouse stocks `n` products. Every product is packed in boxes of the same physical size, so each box takes exactly one slot of truck space, but products differ in how many units a single box holds. For product `i` there are `boxes[i]` boxes available and each box contains `unitsPerBox[i]` units.

The truck can carry at most `truckSize` boxes in total. You may take any number of boxes (from zero up to `boxes[i]`) of each product. Print the maximum total number of units that can be shipped.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `boxes[0] ... boxes[n - 1]`.
The third line contains `n` integers `unitsPerBox[0] ... unitsPerBox[n - 1]`.
The fourth line contains the integer `truckSize`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum number of units.

examples.explanation: The truck holds 3 boxes. Take the single 3-unit box, then the two 2-unit boxes: 3 + 2 + 2 = 7. The third product would only add boxes worth 1 unit and the truck is already full.
Take boxes from the richest products first: 5 boxes of 10 units (50), 3 boxes of 7 units (21), then the remaining 2 slots with 5-unit boxes (10). Total 81.
The truck is larger than the stock, so everything is shipped: 2 * 4 + 2 * 9 = 26.

hints: Every box uses one slot, so a box with more units is always at least as good as one with fewer.
Sort the products by units per box in descending order.
Walk through the sorted products, taking as many boxes as still fit (`min(boxes, remaining)`), and stop when the truck is full.
